components: an inner stem and its rounded bowl
a right upright standing on the low bar
strokeOrder: start at the top of the left upright and draw it straight down
without lifting, climb back up it and carry the top bar to its right end
without lifting, come back along the bar to the inner stem and draw it down to its foot
without lifting, go back up the stem and round the bowl down to the low bar
without lifting, run left along the low bar to its end
without lifting, come back along the low bar and climb the right upright — and only now lift
strokeOrderNote: one continuous stroke — six joined movements, no pen lift; it goes back up the left upright and the inner stem, and back along the top bar and the low bar; stroke count, order and direction from native writers' pen traces in HP Labs India's LipiTk Tamil recognizer, class 13, overriding the order and the lift of Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I, Frame 2, ங

strokeOrderSource.citation: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 2, ங (University of Texas at Austin), p. 191; reordered, and drawn in one stroke, after HP Labs India, Lipi Toolkit, Lipi Indic Character Recognizers 4.0, Tamil recognizer, class 13 (ங): stored online-handwriting prototypes from native writers (MIT licence, 2012)
strokeOrderSource.variation: Appendix I Frame 2 draws ங's right upright first, downward, as a detached part, and then the body after a lift. Native writers draw ங in one stroke and draw that upright last. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 92 of the 108 stored prototypes of ங (85%) are one pen-down stroke. 75 of the 92 (82%) start at the upper left, and 69 (75%) go down the left upright and climb back up it before moving right; 81 (88%) draw the right upright upward at the end, and 73 (79%) end at the top right. So this ductus overrides Frame 2's order and its lift. The bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline joins the right upright to the low bar at its foot, carries the top bar past the inner stem, hangs the bowl from the stem above the stem's free foot, and carries the low bar left under the stem, so the pen goes down the left upright and back up it, out along the top bar and back to the inner stem, down the stem to its foot and back up into the bowl, round the bowl to the low bar, out to the low bar's left end and back, and up the right upright. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the stroke count, the start, the order and the direction, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline. The underlying HP Labs data is licensed for research use only, so only counts and shares are cited here, and no trace was copied. Tamil handwriting varies by school.

notes: Nga is the nasal partner of க: it supplies the ṅ sound in clusters such as ங்க. Native writers draw it in one stroke and draw the right upright last, upward; Frame 2's detached first upright is a teaching split, and in Noto Sans Tamil that upright stands on the low bar at the right.
